relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR smart-followup treats a shared scheduling/Calendly link as a booked meeting → drops warm leads from reminders
relatedSnapshot.description:
Source: Raindrop CRITICAL issue Shared scheduling links treated as booked meetings (75 events, 58 users, 7d). Surfaced in the Jul 12 2026 Raindrop Daily Summary. Validated independently by the Raindrop Alert Processor.

## Symptom

When a prospect shares their OWN scheduling link (Calendly/calendar) or asks the sender to schedule, the `smart-followup` agent (`google/gemini-2.5-flash`, agent_id `<uuid>`, prompt v2) sets `requires_followup: false` and ends the sequence, citing a successful booking. No meeting time was ever confirmed, so an interested lead is silently dropped from the reminder sequence.

## Root cause (verified in code)

`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/agents/smart-followup/default-agent.ts` — the system prompt's "Name 4 are NOT Required" list (lines 17-22) includes:

```
- Meeting was successfully booked (calendar handles reminders)
```

There is no guidance distinguishing a confirmed slot from (a) a prospect sharing their own scheduling link, or (b) a "you go ahead and book it" handoff. The model equates any link-based scheduling gesture with a completed booking. Matches Raindrop's root-cause hypothesis exactly.

## Firsthand evidence

Event `<uuid>` (convo `<uuid>`, podcast campaign). Prospect merely sent their calendar link; agent output:

```json
{"requires_followup":false,"next_follow_up_date_iso":null,"followup_sequence":[],"reason":"Meeting was successfully booked (prospect sent their calendar link) - no follow-up needed."}
```

Corroborating stumbles today: agent cancels follow-up after prospect shares scheduling link, assistant ignored the user's booking link after saying Understood.

## Trend (adversarial note)

Issue-matched events peaked Jul 9 (25/day) and declined through Jul 11 (5/day); the headline "58 users" is a 7-day cumulative, not a single-day spike. Still real and recurring (today's stumbles confirm). Impact is high because the failure is silent — a genuinely interested lead is dropped with no reminder and no human flag.

## Suggested fix direction

In the smart-followup prompt, explicitly state that a shared scheduling link or a "you book it" handoff is NOT a confirmed booking and DOES require a follow-up (treat like "slots proposed, no confirmation"). Only suppress follow-ups when a specific time is confirmed. Overlaps with the broader prompt rework in ENG-8385; predecessor ENG-6398 (copywriter booking-link confusion) was canceled.

Owner via git blame: prompt block authored by Koppany Kondricz.

relatedSnapshot.title: Native out-of-order webhook tolerance: meeting_booked without reply_received
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Sub-ticket 2 of 6 for** ENG-10036 **(Hardening 4). Blocked by webhook idempotency (**ENG-10043**). Coordinate with in-flight** ENG-8214 **— this ticket absorbs/re-scopes it; do not build a parallel competing fix.**

## Problem

Company One sometimes sends `lead_meeting_booked` with NO preceding `reply_received` (observed 9–33h delays between related events — ENG-8214). Routing historically only handled the `reply_received`-first ordering, so confirmations were missed and meeting invites never sent. The first fix attempt **synthesized fake** `reply_received` **events** and was rejected in QA with 6 reproduced bugs: duplicate workflow runs, `new Date()` overwriting real provider timestamps, dropped meeting metadata, empty workspace field.

## Build notes — handle the event natively, do not synthesize

* In `routeOutreachWebhookEvent` / `inngest-routing.ts`, give `lead_meeting_booked` a first-class handling path that does not assume a prior `reply_received`:
  * Resolve-or-create the thread idempotently (the idempotency layer from ENG-10043 makes this safe).
  * Use **provider timestamps from the payload**, never `new Date()` — this was QA bug #2 last time.
  * Preserve all meeting metadata from the event (QA bug #3) and workspace/org fields (QA bug #4).
  * Booking path must guard against duplicate active appointments (existing v2 rule) — late-arriving `reply_received` for the same booking must not double-process (idempotency key + thread-state check).
* Lifecycle: `booked` transition through `updateLifecycle` with proper history; remember the `booked↔replied` oscillation race from ENG-8139 — a late `reply_received` arriving AFTER `meeting_booked` must not regress lifecycle backwards.
* Read ENG-8214's comment thread first: Name 7's QA repro steps are the acceptance test script; Name 5/Name 6's RCA has payload examples.
* Tests: webhook routing tests with out-of-order sequences (booked-first, reply-late, duplicates of each).

## Acceptance criteria

* `meeting_booked`-first ordering produces a correct booked thread + invite flow with provider timestamps and full metadata.
* The 6 QA failure modes from the rejected fix each have a regression test.
* Late `reply_received` after `meeting_booked`: no duplicate run, no lifecycle regression.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR rebooks lost meetings and reconfirms meetings booked days ahead
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a booked meeting falls through, the AI offers to rebook the same day, with fresh times. Meetings booked 3 or more days out get a short reconfirmation the day before. Today 88% of lost meetings never get a message, and meetings booked far ahead are lost more often.

## Problem

* About 160 AI SDR meetings a week are lost after booking: the prospect declines the invite, the event is removed, or it is cancelled in a synced calendar.
* 88% of those threads get no message within 14 days, and only 1.9% rebook. The thread usually still says "booked", which blocks follow-ups.
* Meetings booked 5 or more days ahead are lost at about 20%, against about 12% for meetings under 3 days away. Nothing reconfirms them.

## User experience

* **Prospect declines or cancels:** within an hour, in the same thread and from the same sender, they get a short note: "no problem, here are a few other times", with live times, or "tell me a day that suits".
  * One reminder 4 days later if they don't reply, then stop.
  * The thread's status changes from "booked" back to "times offered".
* **The host removed the event** (it may be on our side): the deal owner and workspace owner get an alert first, and no email goes to the prospect until someone confirms it should.
* **Meeting booked 3 or more days out:** about 24 hours before, the prospect gets a two-line confirmation:
  * the meeting time in their time zone;
  * "reply here if you need to move it".

  Nothing is sent for meetings booked less than 3 days out, or ones already cancelled.

## What's included

1. **Lost-meeting trigger.** When an AI SDR appointment becomes cancelled or rejected:
   * Prospect-side (rejected invite, cancelled by the prospect) and not a reschedule: reset the thread from "booked", then send the rebook email using the winning writer arm with situation `MEETING_LOST`, with live times (as in ENG-14760). Schedule one follow-up 4 days later.
   * Host-side ("event removed from the host's calendar"): alert the owners, and create a CRM task to decide.
2. **Reconfirmation job.** On AI SDR appointment creation, if the meeting is 3 or more days away, sleep until 24 hours before. Check it's still scheduled, then send the confirmation, written by code from a fixed template with the time filled in by code. No model.
3. Both go through the same validator: do-not-contact, AI SDR enabled, workspace active, human takeover.
4. Each has its own switch per workspace (default on), and both are counted in the weekly report: rebook rate, and show-up rate where attendance is known.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14758: the new writer and its checks, used for the rebook email.
* ENG-14760: live times, used in the rebook email.

## Done when

- [ ] In preview, declining an AI SDR invite produces a rebook email with live times within an hour, and the thread is no longer "booked".
- [ ] A host-side removal creates an owner alert and task, and sends no prospect email.
- [ ] A reschedule (old appointment superseded by a new one) triggers nothing.
- [ ] A meeting booked 4 days out gets exactly one confirmation about 24 hours before, with the correct local time. A meeting booked 1 day out gets none. A meeting cancelled before the reminder time gets none.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests cover each path above.

## Implementation context

* Plan and evidence: AI SDR Follow-ups v2
* Supersedes ENG-8381 (configurable meeting reminders) for AI SDR meetings.
* Triggers, status values and tests are in this ticket's AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Use Claude as model for all SDR related agents.
AI SDR follow-ups offer live, code-filled meeting times
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Follow-ups can offer real, currently free meeting times again. The model never types a time: it leaves a placeholder, and code fills it with live slots from the host's calendar, in the prospect's time zone, right before sending. If the prospect then replies "the first one works", it books.

## Problem

* Since 11 Sep, follow-ups can't offer times. That ban came after follow-ups invented dates: 109 of 363 dated follow-ups named a date already in the past.
* The times our earlier reply offered have usually passed by the time we follow up: in 72% of second follow-ups and 98% of third follow-ups, every offered time had gone.
* Prospects who revive mostly propose a time or ask us to resend times, so a follow-up with fresh times removes a round trip.

## User experience

* A prospect who was offered times and went quiet gets a follow-up with 2 or 3 new, currently free times for the same call, in their own time zone, plus "or tell me a day that suits".
* If they reply with one of those times, the AI books it exactly as it books times from a normal reply.
* If the host has no free time, the follow-up is written without times ("want me to send a couple of options?"), never with made-up ones.
* If the times we offered earlier are gone because the host's calendar filled up, the follow-up can say so truthfully ("those filled up, here are a few new ones"). If they're gone only because the dates passed, it just offers new times without giving a reason.

## What's included

1. **Live slot fetch** at send time, reusing the deterministic part of today's slot matching:
   * the campaign's host calendar
   * the call type
   * free slots
   * business hours
   * 3 spread-out slots in the prospect's time zone
2. **The** `{{TIMES}}` **placeholder.** It becomes allowed in the writer prompt (`fresh_times_available: yes` when at least 2 slots are free), and code replaces it with the formatted slots.
3. **Record the offered slots** exactly as a normal reply does: a slot-matchmaking record with the proposed slots, and the thread moved to "slots sent". The next reply's booking then recognises "the first one works".
4. **Final checks** on the rendered email:
   * every time in it is one of the fetched slots;
   * no slot starts within 12 hours.
   * If fewer than 2 slots are free at render time, regenerate once with `fresh_times_available: no`. If that also fails the checks, skip the follow-up.
5. **Ships as a new writer version (arm)** with the same prompt plus times, so its effect is measured on its own.
6. **Taken or passed.** Before writing, code sorts each time we offered earlier into one of three groups:
   * **passed:** it now starts less than 12 hours from now, so it can't be booked;
   * **taken:** it's still in the future, but it's no longer in the host's free slots;
   * **still open:** it's still free.

   The writer gets `offered_times_taken: yes` only when nothing is still open and at least one time was taken. Only then may it say the earlier times filled up. A final check rejects "filled up", "booked up", "snapped up", "got taken" and similar wording in any other case, because that would be invented scarcity, which the prompt bans.

No calendar holds: the normal booking step already re-checks availability when the prospect picks a time.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14758: the new writer, placeholders and checks.

## Done when

- [ ] In preview, a follow-up on a thread whose offered times have all passed shows 3 new free times from the host calendar in the prospect's time zone.
- [ ] Replying "the first one works" to that follow-up books the first slot (preview end to end).
- [ ] With the host calendar fully blocked, the follow-up goes out without times, or is skipped, and never shows a made-up time.
- [ ] When a time we offered earlier has since been taken on the host calendar, the follow-up may say those times filled up. When the times only passed, it gives no reason. Unit tests cover the passed, taken and still-open groups, and the check that rejects "filled up" wording unless `offered_times_taken` is yes.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: slot formatting across time zones and daylight-saving, the 12-hour minimum notice, the "fewer than 2 slots" path, and the check that every rendered time is a fetched slot.
- [ ] The times version runs as its own arm, and the weekly report shows it separately.

## Implementation context

* Plan and evidence: AI SDR Follow-ups v2
* Related: ENG-14743 (scheduling context on replies) and ENG-13492 (the 11 Sep ban this replaces).
* Exact functions to reuse and the tests are in this ticket's AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Question replies answer the question and offer verified meeting times
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a prospect asks a question, the AI SDR answers it but almost never offers a time to talk, and in workspaces whose knowledge base requires slots the reply can be dropped entirely. Scope widened on 6 Oct 2026 under ENG-14763: every question reply should answer the question and offer verified meeting times, unless a meeting is already booked.

Original report: when a prospect simply asks a question the AI SDR knowledge base can answer, the reply can be dropped entirely: copy review rejects the automated reply on two mutually exclusive grounds and the workflow escalates with nothing sent.

## Problem

An inbound reply routed to the question path never gets an answer. The thread shows "Escalated for Review" with no draft, and a person has to notice it and reply by hand. Threads that were answered and threads that were withheld look the same to the operator until the thread is opened.

## Wider gap (added 6 Oct 2026)

In the last 7 days of AI drafts, only 7% of question-route replies contained specific meeting times, against 98% on the booking route and 93% on the positive route. The question route never fetches calendar slots, so it can only suggest "a quick chat". James decided on 6 Oct that classifying an interested reply as a question is fine as long as the question route answers and offers times, and that a real question must always be answered.

## Root cause

On the question route the workflow never computes calendar slots, while a workspace's MANDATORY knowledge-base rules are injected into both the copywriter and the copy-review context packs as highest priority and can require the reply to offer verified slots. Both outputs available to the copywriter are then rejected — inventing times fails as an unverified booking claim, and answering without times fails as not offering slots — and after COPY_REVIEW_MAX_ATTEMPTS the workflow escalates instead of sending.

* apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/workflow.ts — executeSlotMatchmakingStep runs only inside the BOOKING/RESCHEDULE branches; the QUESTION branch runs the knowledge step only, so no slots ever reach the copywriter.
* apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/helpers/context-pack-helpers/reply-directive.ts — generateQuestionDirective emits ANSWER with no offered times.
* apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/helpers/context-pack.ts — formatCombinedKnowledge emits the workspace rules as "### MANDATORY RULES (HIGHEST PRIORITY — override all other knowledge)" into both packs.
* apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/helpers/copywriter-with-review.ts — retries to COPY_REVIEW_MAX_ATTEMPTS, then sets escalate with "Copy review failed after N attempts", so nothing is sent.
* apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/helpers/copy-review-policy.ts — question_fabrication is a BLOCKING_TYPE, and the reviewer recorded a missing-slots finding as question_fabrication although nothing was fabricated.

## Blast radius

Measured 2026-09-24 in production over a trailing 60-day window. Confirmed affected and potentially exposed are separate figures.

* Confirmed affected, strict signature (rejection names the mandated or required slots): 3 runs in 1 organization. Looser "correctly answers the question but fails to offer slots or times" pattern: 4 runs across 2 organizations, the second of which also carried a separate fabrication finding.
* Potentially exposed, a question-route reply blocked by copy review citing slots or availability in either direction: 105 runs across 81 organizations.
* Upper bound, any copy-review block on a question-route thread (causes vary, including genuine fabrication catches): 959 runs across 412 organizations.

Method: production execution_runs where status is escalated and the final rejection matches the copy-review-failure pattern, joined on thread to the same run's intent-classification row routed to QUESTION. The confirmed tier is text-matched on stored rejection wording, so it undercounts unanticipated phrasing.

## Proposed fix

Fetch verified calendar slots on the question route and pass them to the reply writer, so every question reply answers from the knowledge base and offers a few verified times, unless a meeting is already booked on the thread. This also removes the root cause above: a mandatory knowledge-base rule that requires slots can now be met. A missing booking offer must never be recorded as a fabrication block, and a reply that answers the question must be sent rather than escalated.

## What's included

Scope: the question-route reply path from directive generation through copy review to send or escalate. Separately filed work: none required. Not applicable: no containment or customer-recovery work, because every known affected thread already has a later outbound reply.

## Regression seam

Public boundary: an inbound reply routed to the question path in a workspace whose rules require verified slots alongside the answer. Red before: the run ends escalated with "Copy review failed after 2 attempts" and no outbound row. Green after: the reply is sent carrying the knowledge-base answer, with only verified times if any are offered.

## Done when

* Question-route replies include the answer and verified meeting times, unless a meeting is already booked.
* A question-route reply in a workspace whose rules mandate offering slots is sent rather than escalated, with the knowledge-base answer included.
* A missing booking offer on the answer route no longer blocks the copy and is never recorded as a fabrication.
* A regression test proves the red-before, green-after behaviour at that seam.
* One week after release, the share of sent question replies with specific times is reported to James (baseline 7%).

## Reports

* ENG-14206

relatedSnapshot.title: Count calendar-synced campaign meetings only after an interested reply
relatedSnapshot.description:
Part of ENG-10978 (metrics rework). This ticket now captures the stricter calendar-sync eligibility rule confirmed on 28 August 2026.

## Outcome

A Name 8 or Outlook calendar event only counts as a campaign meeting when the attendee is the same campaign lead who genuinely replied and was classified as interested by the outreach provider.

## Problem

Calendar sync currently materialises a campaign booking whenever an attendee email matches a lead in one of the calendar owner's organisations. It does not first require a reply or an interested classification. The dashboard later counts those records for active campaigns, so unrelated client meetings and pre-existing calendar events can inflate “meetings booked.”

Current lead status is not safe proof: marking a meeting booked can itself cascade the lead to Reply Received and Interested.

## Required behaviour

* Match the attendee to a lead in the exact organisation and campaign.
* Require provider webhook evidence for that same provider campaign and lead email:
  * a genuine `reply_received` event; and
  * a genuine `lead_interested` event.
* For EmailBison, a `TAG_ATTACHED` event normalised as interested is not sufficient evidence. This prevents the Meeting Booked tag from proving its own eligibility.
* AI SDR inferred positive replies do not satisfy this calendar-sync rule; the positive classification must come from the campaign provider.
* If either item of evidence is missing, skip campaign booking attribution entirely: do not create the calendar-derived external booking, appointment, or CRM “booked” lifecycle transition.
* Because provider reply webhooks can arrive just after the calendar event, recheck eligibility after 1, 5, and 15 minutes. Each recheck must reload the live provider event, stop for deleted or cancelled events, and use the same strict evidence gate.
* Existing linked booking updates, cancellations, reschedules, and retry/idempotency behaviour remain unchanged.
* Active-campaign filtering in the existing dashboard metric remains unchanged in this focused fix.
* Historical false-positive booking records are not deleted or backfilled by this change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A calendar attendee who matches a campaign lead but has no provider reply/interested evidence does not create a campaign booking.
2. A replied lead without a genuine interested event does not create a campaign booking.
3. An EmailBison `TAG_ATTACHED`/Meeting Booked tag cannot qualify the lead.
4. A lead with both genuine provider `reply_received` and genuine provider `lead_interested` evidence in the same campaign still creates exactly one booking through the existing flow.
5. Evidence is scoped by organisation, provider, provider campaign ID, and normalised lead email.
6. Focused automated tests cover the rejected and accepted paths.
7. No schema migration or production-data mutation is included.

relatedSnapshot.title: Integrate booking links properly into the AI SDR
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let the AI SDR handle booking links both ways: send the host's link when a prospect asks, and answer prospects who send their own. We're doing this so more interested prospects book a meeting, and so nothing gives away that a machine is writing.

About 44 prospects a week ask the AI SDR for a booking link, and today it has none to send, so it offers times again. Those threads book within 7 days only 40.5% of the time on podcast campaigns and 28.1% on direct, against 87.5% when a prospect picks one of our times.

## Problem

Three things go wrong today, and each child fixes one. The diagram shows where.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Prospect asks for link] --> B["(2) Reply: link and times"]
  C[Prospect sends own link] --> D["(3) Reply and host task"]
  B --> E[Prospect or host books]
  D --> E
  E --> F["(1) Booking stops follow-ups"]
```

Each number is the child that changes that step.

1. A booking only stops follow-ups when Company One or EmailBison also marked the lead "interested", and a follow-up can go out before the calendar update arrives. One follow-up after a booking shows the prospect that a machine is writing.
2. The AI SDR has no booking link to send, even though 22% of active AI SDR workspaces keep one in their knowledge base.
3. When a prospect sends their own scheduling link, the thread goes to a person and the prospect gets no reply. That happened 78 times in 4 weeks.

## User experience

* A prospect who asks for our calendar gets the host's link with two times, in one reply.
* A prospect who sends their own link hears back within minutes, and the host gets a one-click task to book it.
* Whoever books, and however they book, follow-ups stop straight away and the thread shows as booked.
* Workspace owners see a new "Booking link" field on each meeting type.

## What's included

1. Stop follow-ups once a prospect books through any tool.
2. Let the AI SDR send the host's booking link.
3. Answer prospects who send their own scheduling link, and hand the booking to the host.

## Out of scope

* A direct Calendly integration (connecting Calendly, moving deals from it, and letting the AI SDR book through it): that's a separate master.
* Booking through a prospect's link with browser automation, because it's too error-prone for about 20 threads a week.
* Our own hosted booking page.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Waves show the earliest point a ticket can start, not a barrier.

### Wave 1: can start now

1. ENG-14786: stop follow-ups once a prospect books through any tool.

### Wave 2: starts when ENG-14786 is done

Parallel: ENG-14788 and ENG-14789. They both touch the reply-instruction code, so agree who changes it first.

2. ENG-14788: send the host's booking link. Blocked by ENG-14786.
3. ENG-14789: answer prospects' own links. Blocked by ENG-14786.

Cross-wave overlap: none.

## How we'll measure

* **Link asks that book.** Base: AI SDR threads where the prospect asked for our calendar or booking link, booked within 7 days, from the follow-up results report. Today it's 40.5% on podcast campaigns and 28.1% on direct. We'll aim toward the 87.5% of prospects who pick an offered time. We'll read it 4 weeks after the second child ships.
* **Follow-ups sent after a booking.** Base: follow-ups sent while the thread had a booking on the host calendar, from the first child's cancel log. Target: zero once it ships. We can't count today's value, because nothing logs it yet.

## Done when

* All three children are merged and released.
* The link-ask booking rate is posted on this ticket 4 weeks after the second child ships.

## Implementation context

* Research and plan: Booking Links and Calendly.
* Replaces ENG-14779, which is marked a duplicate of this ticket.
* Related: ENG-14756 (follow-ups v2), ENG-14760 (live times in follow-ups), ENG-14761 (rebook lost meetings), ENG-11624 (today's hand-off for prospects' own links), ENG-11714 (the earlier design for the reply to a prospect's own link), ENG-12059 (call length mismatch).

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR booking links: send ours, handle the prospect's own, and stop follow-ups the moment anyone books
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Three changes so booking feels human:

1. The AI SDR can send the host's own booking link (Calendly, <domain>, HubSpot or any link) when a prospect asks for one, and offer it as an "or book here" option next to times.
2. When a prospect sends *their* scheduling link, the AI replies straight away like a person would, and the host gets a one-click task to book it.
3. Whenever a prospect books through any tool, follow-ups stop. A follow-up after someone has booked is the clearest sign that a machine is writing, so this part ships first.

## Problem

* **About 44 prospects a week ask for our booking link.** The AI has no link to send, so it offers times again. Those threads book 40% (podcast) and 28% (direct) of the time, against 88% when a prospect picks one of our times. Most workspaces already have a link: one sits in the knowledge base for 60% of podcast threads and 35% of direct threads.
* **When a prospect sends their own scheduling link, nobody answers them.** Since ENG-11624 the AI escalates the thread to the client (78 runs in 4 weeks). It sends the prospect nothing, and escalated warm threads usually sit unanswered for days.
* **Follow-ups can still go out after someone books.** We already watch the host's Name 8 or Outlook calendar and cancel follow-ups when a prospect's booking appears (158 follow-ups cancelled in the last 28 days). It has two gaps:
  * the follow-up can be sent before the calendar update arrives;
  * the rule depends on Company One or EmailBison marking the lead "interested". That mark is present for about 94% of replied threads, so the other 6% are missed, and so is any provider that doesn't send it.

## User experience

**Workspace owner (settings):**

* Each meeting type gets an optional **Booking link** field. A campaign can override it, for teams where each host has their own link.
* If the knowledge base already contains a scheduler link, the field shows it as a suggestion. It is never filled in silently.

**Prospect asks for a link:** "Can you just send me your calendar?"

* The AI replies with the link, plus the times it would have offered.
* It never says it can't send a link.

**Prospect is offered times:** after the times, one line: "Or if it's easier, grab any time here: <link>". This line is tested 50/50 by thread (see Open questions).

**Prospect sends their own link:** "Just grab a time here: calendly.com/…"

* The AI replies within minutes: "Perfect, I'll grab a time on your calendar." It never names a time.
* At the same moment, the host gets a CRM task and a notification: "<Prospect> asked you to book via their link", with the link and two times the host is free.
* When the booking appears on the host's calendar, the thread is marked booked and the task closes itself.
* If the task is still open after one business day, the host gets a reminder. The AI sends no follow-ups while this is waiting.

**Prospect books by any route** (our link, their link, a forwarded invite): follow-ups stop, the booking shows on the thread, and the follow-up row records why it was cancelled.

## What's included

Two pull requests on this ticket, in this order.

**PR 1: stop follow-ups once anyone books. Ships first, no prospect-facing change.**

1. **Match on our own data, not the provider's label.** In the calendar-sync booking detection, a calendar attendee counts as a prospect booking when *either* of these holds:
   * the existing provider evidence (a reply plus an "interested" event);
   * **or** the prospect has sent us at least one real reply (not an auto-reply) in an AI SDR thread in this workspace. Any reply counts: interested, question, objection or not-now.
2. **Check right before each follow-up sends:**
   * Look for a booking with this prospect: our own appointments and tracked external bookings, plus a live look at the host's connected calendar for the next 60 days.
   * If the prospect, or another attendee from the same company email domain, is on an event created since our first reply in the thread, cancel the follow-up as `already_booked_external`.
   * Never match on shared mail domains such as gmail.com or outlook.com.
3. **Outcome logging:** every cancel records which check caught it, so we can see how much each part helps.

**PR 2: booking links**

4. **Booking link setting:** on meeting types, with a campaign override. https only, checked on save.
5. **Reply path:**
   * **Prospect asks for a link:** send the link and offer times. The writer can only insert the link as a code-filled placeholder and never types the URL itself.
   * **Fallback line next to offered times:** on for half of new threads (stable by thread), off for the other half.
6. **Follow-up writer:** allow `{{LINK:booking}}` in follow-ups. Use it in the "times passed" follow-up and whenever the prospect asked for a link. This needs one line in prompt v3 and an allowed-links entry.
7. **Prospect's own link:**
   * Replace today's escalation with three things: the acknowledgement reply, the host task with the link and two free times, and the notification.
   * Only send the reply once the task and the notification have both been created. If either fails, escalate as today and send nothing.
   * Keep the link as structured data on the thread, not only in a text reason.
8. **Activation tracking:** the new booking-link setting gets PostHog events through the repo's `instrument-activation-tracking` skill.

**Not included:**

* booking through the prospect's link by browser automation (too error-prone for about 20 threads a week);
* a direct Calendly connection (later, if links prove they book more);
* our own hosted booking page.

## Done when

- [ ] PR 1: a prospect who books through any tool on the host's connected calendar has every pending follow-up cancelled, including when the sending tool never marked them "interested" (integration test plus one preview run).
- [ ] PR 1: a follow-up due 1 minute after a booking lands is cancelled by the pre-send check, not sent (integration test).
- [ ] PR 1: an attendee from the same company domain cancels follow-ups; a gmail.com attendee does not (unit tests).
- [ ] PR 2: with a booking link set, "can you send me your calendar?" gets the link plus times. With no link set, behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] PR 2: a prospect who sends their own Calendly link gets the acknowledgement reply, the host gets the task and notification, and the thread turns booked when the event lands on the host calendar (preview, end to end).
- [ ] PR 2: if task creation fails, no reply is sent and the thread escalates as today.
- [ ] PR 2: the fallback-line split is stable per thread, and the follow-up results report shows bookings and replies for each half.
- [ ] Browser QA of the setting (save, validation error, suggestion from the knowledge base), with PostHog events verified landing.

## Open questions

* **Should the "or book here" line go on every offer, or be tested first?** Recommended default: test it 50/50 for 4 weeks. Our data shows follow-ups carrying non-booking links got about 13.5 points fewer replies, possibly a spam-filter effect. Booking-link follow-ups showed about 6 points fewer, but that is understated, because link bookings were never counted. Sending the link when the prospect *asks* is not in question and is on for everyone.
* **Who gets the "book via their link" task when the campaign has no host?** Recommended default: the deal owner, then the workspace owner.

## Implementation context

* Plan and research: AI SDR Follow-ups v2. Follow-up programme: ENG-14756.
* The earlier design for the prospect's-own-link reply, including the "only reply once the task exists" rule: ENG-11714, closed as a duplicate of ENG-11624, which only built the escalation.
* A meeting-type link also fixes the length mismatch in ENG-12059 when the meeting type and link agree.
* Exact files, rules, queries and tests are in this ticket's AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: A cancelled meeting still counts as booked
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Simple outcome

If a customer's only future meeting is cancelled, CRM treats them as having no meeting booked so they return to the rep's follow-up list.

---

## Overview

A contact whose only meeting was cancelled still shows as having a meeting scheduled, so they drop out of the follow-up lists that exist to catch exactly that situation.

## Problem

A rep books a meeting, the prospect cancels, and the CRM keeps treating that contact as booked. Filtering for people with no meeting scheduled skips them, which is the opposite of what a rep needs: a cancelled meeting is the strongest reason to reach out again.

It goes wrong in two separate ways. The booking itself is still counted even after it is cancelled, and the conversation is left marked as booked, so both routes report a meeting that is not happening.

## Proposed fix

Stop counting cancelled bookings, on both routes, so "has a meeting scheduled" means a meeting that is actually still on the books.

## What's included

Both halves of the check, at both the person and deal level.

Not included: the other appointment filters, which already handle cancellations correctly and are the reference for what "still on the books" should mean.

## Blocked by

None: complete and in review.

## How it should work

A contact whose only future meeting is cancelled reports no meeting scheduled. "Has a meeting" and "has no meeting" stay exact opposites, with nobody in both and nobody in neither.

## Who can do what

No permission change.

## What the user sees

Contacts whose meeting was cancelled reappear in the lists reps use to chase people without a meeting booked. Existing saved views using this filter return a different set afterwards.

## Done when

- [ ] A contact whose only future meeting is cancelled reports no meeting scheduled, at both the person and deal level.
- [ ] A conversation left marked as booked by a cancelled meeting does not report one either.
- [ ] "Has a meeting" and "has no meeting" remain exact opposites.
- [ ] Database-backed coverage for both routes.
- [ ] The change to existing saved views is called out at review with a row count.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

A cancelled meeting puts the contact back on the list of people to chase, where they belong.

## Implementation context

Delivered by Acquisity/Acquisity#6079.

This was deliberately left out of the deal-grain work rather than overlooked. That change's job was to add a grain, and this filter is already saved into live contact views, so narrowing it there would have silently re-answered existing views inside a change meant only to extend one. It was carried across unchanged instead, so the two grains could not disagree, and the gap was recorded rather than hidden.

Worth noting the distinction that decided the split. That PR did widen a related check, because it was matching nobody at all in production, which moves contacts from a wrong answer to a right one. This change moves contacts the other way on a check that already works, which is a redefinition and earns its own QA pass.

When implementing, confirm the exact cancelled status values in the schema, and check whether rescheduling leaves the old booking cancelled with a new one beside it.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR follow-ups v2: smarter follow-ups that book more meetings
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Rebuild the AI SDR's automatic follow-up emails so they book more meetings. Prospects who replied once and then went quiet will get short follow-ups that know what we already said, offer real times, and fit their situation. The writer switches to Claude Sonnet 5.5 for every follow-up at once, and we measure the result before against after. After that, new prompt versions can be tested side by side and improved every few weeks.

## Problem

* Follow-ups matter: when they were skipped because a cold campaign was paused, first-follow-up replies were about 26% against 3.6% without, and 14-day bookings about 8% against 2%. That points to roughly 80 to 90 meetings a week coming from follow-ups today.
* But today's follow-ups are mostly "just checking in" notes:
  * The writer sees every email we sent earlier as blank, so it repeats itself, thanks people for replies they never sent and claims links it never sent.
  * It gets no sender, offer, show, host, title, company or today's date.
  * Since 11 Sep it can't offer times, and by the second follow-up every time we offered has usually passed (72%).
* A Gemini 2.5 Flash scheduler decides who gets follow-ups. It copies its own prompt example 89% of the time, and it skips 24% of threads where we offered times, mostly by wrongly deciding the prospect already booked.
* Some threads get nothing at all:
  * paused campaigns
  * out-of-office replies
  * "check back next week"
  * lost meetings: 88% never get a rebook message

## User experience

* A prospect who said "sounds good" and then went quiet gets a short email from the same sender, in the same thread. It recaps the one thing they asked about and offers real, currently free times, or asks them to name a day.
* A prospect who said "try me next week" hears back next week, quoting their reason.
* A prospect whose meeting got cancelled gets a same-day offer to rebook.
* Threads that need a human, such as a prospect who sent their own booking link, go to the deal owner as a task instead of getting an AI email.
* Workspace owners notice nothing changing in the product. They see more replies and booked calls.

## What's included

Five child tickets, each one PR:

1. **Testing setup for the follow-up writer:** versions, A/B assignment (for later prompt tests), full logging and a before/after results report. Plus the policy switches:
   * follow-ups keep going when a campaign is paused by hand;
   * short deferrals get a follow-up;
   * out-of-office replies no longer wipe the sequence.
2. **The new writer:** Claude Sonnet 5.5 on a dedicated follow-up prompt. James decided on 6 Oct to switch it on for 100% of follow-ups in one step, after a 14-day baseline, and measure before against after.
3. **Live meeting times:** filled in by code, in follow-ups.
4. **A rules engine** that replaces the Gemini scheduler, with Claude Sonnet 5.5 for odd cases, tested against the old scheduler. It also handles the "our calendar has no slots" alert and one email to a new address the prospect names.
5. **Meeting plays:** rebook lost meetings, and reconfirm meetings booked 3 or more days out.

Not included (parked by James on 6 Oct): SMS, call and LinkedIn follow-ups, and paid lead enrichment.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets explicitly grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they still keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none.

* **Priority 1:** AI SDR follow-up writer gets A/B testing and full logging, and warm follow-ups stop dropping off: versions, logging, the before/after results report, the history fix and the three policy switches. Its first 14 days live are the baseline for the new writer.

### Wave 2: starts when ENG-14757 is done

Parallel: ENG-14758 and ENG-14759.

* **Priority 2:** New AI SDR follow-up writer: Sonnet 5.5 on a follow-up-only prompt, switched on for all follow-ups: blocked by ENG-14757.
* **Priority 4:** Rules engine with a Sonnet 5.5 fallback decides which AI SDR threads get follow-ups: blocked by ENG-14757.

### Wave 3: starts when ENG-14758 is done

Parallel: none within the wave.

* **Priority 3:** AI SDR follow-ups offer live, code-filled meeting times: blocked by ENG-14758.

### Wave 4: starts when ENG-14758 and ENG-14760 are done

Parallel: none within the wave.

* **Priority 5:** AI SDR rebooks lost meetings and reconfirms meetings booked days ahead: blocked by ENG-14758 and ENG-14760.

Cross-wave overlap:

* ENG-14759 may overlap ENG-14760 and ENG-14761 if still underway. It changes scheduling in `workflow/steps/followup.ts`; they change rendering, slots and appointment triggers. Coordinate on the slot-matching extraction in ENG-14760.

## Done when

* All five child tickets are merged and released.
* The Sonnet 5.5 writer has run at 100% for at least 4 weeks, and the before/after report (positive replies and bookings, per follow-up step, against the trend line) is posted on ENG-14758.
* Today's Gemini scheduler is switched off.

## Implementation context

* Older overlapping tickets: decided by James on 6 Oct. These are marked as duplicates of the matching new child:
  * ENG-8385, ENG-10041, ENG-10054, ENG-10066, ENG-13859, ENG-13855 and ENG-8381.
  * ENG-11729 stays open for its duplicate-scheduling and ghost-closure fixes; its "circle back next week" part moved to ENG-14757.
* Research, model bake-off and plan: AI SDR Follow-ups v2
* Builds on the reply-check programme ENG-14742:
  * ENG-14743 scheduling context
  * ENG-14744 copywriter facts
  * ENG-14745 reply check
* Every child has its own `AI context.md` with exact files, data and test steps.
* The plan page is shared by link (updated 6 Oct with the Sonnet 5.5 decision and the before/after plan). Ask James if it doesn't open.

relatedSnapshot.title: Lead replies missing from AI SDR inbox with booked meeting
relatedSnapshot.description:
user: <email>

Customer reports that for at least one staffing & recruiting campaign lead (Name 9), a meeting was booked by the AI SDR at Thursday 3pm GMT+1, but the lead's reply that triggered the booking is not visible in the AI SDR inbox.

Observed behavior:

* Lead initially replied "sure lets talk thursday".
* AI SDR suggested times.
* Meeting is booked on Name 8 Calendar for Thursday at 3pm GMT+1, even though that time was not in the original suggestions.
* The AI SDR thread does not show the lead's reply that led to the 3pm booking.
* The AI SDR was about to send a follow-up as if the conversation was still open, despite the meeting already being booked.
* The inbox is an inbox bought inside ai-clients, so the customer cannot access the underlying Gmail/Outlook mailbox directly to see the raw email.
* The "Meeting booked" button in the AI SDR interface does not work for this thread, so it cannot be manually moved to "Meeting Booked".

Expected behavior:

* Any lead reply that the AI SDR uses to book a meeting should be visible in the AI SDR inbox thread.
* Once a meeting is booked, the conversation should be marked as booked and no further automated follow-ups should be queued.
* The "Meeting booked" button should be functional so threads can be manually updated when needed.
